Per provider, from Trustpilot (read 2026-11-09). I read the 20 most recent 1-star reviews for each provider, in all languages. Two caveats: that's a small, recent sample, and the "most common complaint" is my own tally of those 20.

NordVPN: TrustScore 4.2, 51,602 reviews (12% are 1-star). Most common complaint: unauthorized charges, surprise auto-renewals and refused refunds (about 9 of 20). Connections that don't work come a close second.

ExpressVPN: 4.4, 29,693 reviews (7% 1-star). Most common complaint: unstable VPN that won't connect or keeps dropping (about 11 of 20). Poor support and slow refunds come next.

Surfshark: 4.3, 31,815 reviews (9% 1-star). Most common complaint: auto-renewal at a higher price, with cancellation made hard and refunds refused (about 11 of 20).

Proton VPN: 2.1, 1,037 reviews (59% 1-star). Most common complaint: billing, meaning silent renewals, refunds turned into credits, and charges after cancelling (about 8 of 20). Slow or failing connections and free-tier limits are nearly as common. A few reviews attack the CEO.

CyberGhost: 4.0, 24,173 reviews (6.6% 1-star). Most common complaint: renewal overcharges and being billed early or at a higher price than advertised (about 10 of 20). Most of these reviews are not in English.

Private Internet Access: 4.2, 11,033 reviews (10% 1-star). Most common complaint: it won't connect, or the dedicated IP, ports or the app are broken (about 10 of 20). Overcharging and refunds are second (about 7 of 20). Its average reply time to negative reviews is about 27 days.

IPVanish: 3.9, 10,307 reviews (6.4% 1-star). Most common complaint: auto-renewal charged without warning or after cancelling (about 14 of 20, the clearest pattern of any provider). I queried it as www.ipvanish.com, the domain key Trustpilot uses.

Mullvad: 3.2, 192 reviews (21% 1-star). Most common complaint: payment problems, such as paying and getting no token or activation, double charges, and lost cash payments (about 8 of 20). Unresponsive support and blocked or non-working connections follow. The profile is unclaimed and has few reviews, so the score is not very reliable.

Fewest serious complaints: ExpressVPN. It has the highest TrustScore (4.4) and one of the lowest 1-star shares (7.1%). Its 1-star reviews are mostly about flaky connections and slow support, not money taken without consent. CyberGhost (6.6%) and IPVanish (6.4%) have slightly lower 1-star shares, but their complaints are almost all about billing, which I'd rate as more serious. ExpressVPN's weak spot is slow replies to negative reviews, about 6 days on average.

{"result": "reduck/search.brave.com/search [none] — Search the web on Brave, one page of results at a time, one query per run. Returns each result's title, url, snippet and date, plus the query as you sent it (not a rewritten one: see operatorsApplied for whether Brave relaxed it). An empty result list means Brave itself found nothing, and the reason is returned in emptyBecause; if the page cannot be read, the script fails with an error instead of returning an empty list.

Search operators (site:, quoted phrases, OR) are supported. site:domain also covers subdomains, and site:domain/path narrows to a path prefix. When too few pages match, Brave drops the operators and runs a looser query; operatorsApplied is then false and the results are not filtered.

Paging: each query has a limited pool of results, and past its end Brave repeats earlier pages. Page while hasMore is true, dedupe by url, and use more specific queries rather than more pages to widen coverage. If Brave rate-limits, the script fails with an error; wait 30 to 60 seconds before retrying.
reduck/chatgpt.com/ask [write] — Open a new ChatGPT chat, send one question, wait for the answer to finish (up to 3 minutes), and return the answer, the sources it cited, and the web searches it ran.

`answers` is a list: ChatGPT sometimes answers twice and asks which reply you prefer, so check its length before reading answers[0]. `references` are the pages the answer cited, each with the id of the search result it came from when ChatGPT gives one (the search call and the result's rank in it). `sources` are the pages its searches gave the model. `searches` and `calls` also list the results ChatGPT shows under Sources but never gave the model, with `given: false`. An empty `references` means that reply cited nothing: the same question may search on one run and not the next, so repeat it before drawing conclusions.

`webSearchQueries` lists what ChatGPT searched for, `searches` groups those queries by round with their results, and `calls` lists each search call with every result's type, position, snippet and date. `activity` gives the progress lines the page showed while it worked ("Searching the web", "Searched 8 websites"). `model`, `stopReason` and `searchContext` say which model answered and how; signed in, `searchContext` also gives the model and thinking effort the account asked for, and its plan.

Signed in, it answers in Chat mode only: when the browser is in Work mode it fails with an error that says so; switch back with set_mode (a Chat choice lasts about four hours). Works signed in or signed out, on a Reduck cloud browser or your own paired browser, in any display language. Signed in, every field is filled, and the account's saved memory can influence the answer. Signed out, ChatGPT shows the answer and its citations but not its searches: `answers`, `references` (with each citation's search result id) and `activity` are filled, and `webSearchQueries`, `searches`, `sources`, `calls`, `model` and `stopReason` are null (unknown, not none).
reduck/claude.ai/ask [write] — Open a new Claude.ai chat, send one question, and wait for the answer to finish (up to 100 s). Returns the answer as the markdown the model emitted, the message and conversation ids, why generation stopped, which model answered, each web search it made with the results it was shown, every source its web_search and web_fetch tools surfaced, and — separately — the sources the answer actually cited. Requires a signed-in session: claude.ai has no anonymous chat, and a signed-out browser fails at once with an error that says so. When the account has used up its 5-hour or weekly allowance, it fails at once with the time the allowance resets, without sending anything. Avoid running many of these at once: claude.ai limits how many chats one account may hold concurrently and refuses the extras, so a refused send comes back quickly carrying Claude's own message and only needs to be retried at a slower pace.
reduck/bing.com/search [none] — Search the web on Bing, one page of results at a time. Returns each organic result's title, url, snippet and date, the market Bing answered for, and where the next page starts.

Results depend on where the browser is: Bing answers for the market of the browser's location, and the answer says which market that was.

To read further, pass the `next` of one answer as `first` of the next call. Pages vary in size and can repeat a result, so dedupe by url.

site: and quoted phrases are passed to Bing as typed; Bing can loosen both, so results may include other sites or pages without the exact phrase. When Bing cannot answer a search, the run fails and says why.
reduck/google.com/search_site [none] — Run a Google search and return one page of organic results (title, url, site, byline, meta, snippet), with Google's link wrappers resolved to the destination url. Results can be personalized to the browser's Google account and location. Narrow queries return the same results in the same order on replay; very broad ones may reorder. For more coverage, fetch several pages or split the query (different site: paths, phrases, or freshness windows), and dedupe by url. An empty list means Google found nothing; when Google shows its anti-bot check, the run fails and says so.
reduck/linkedin.com/search_people [none] — Search LinkedIn people by keywords with optional title, name, company, school, currentCompanyIds/pastCompanyIds (numeric ids from get_company_info), connectionDegrees, connectionOf, geoUrn, and a page number (10 people per page). Returns page, total, hasNextPage and people (name, url, publicId, memberUrn, degree, headline, location, snippet, followers, the mutual-connections line, and the members in common as data: up to two named mutuals with their profile, and mutualCount).

Members in common: each 2nd-degree card names up to two of the people who connect you, and mutualCount says how many there are. To list them all, pass the card's memberUrn as connectionOf. Works alone or with any other filter.

Empty results: people is [] and total is 0 only when LinkedIn shows its empty state. When LinkedIn shows another page instead of results (the monthly search limit of a free account, a security check), the run fails and names what the page showed.

Location: this script takes LinkedIn geo ids only. To search a place, call suggest_locations with the place name first, then pass the geoUrn of the suggestion you want.
reduck/reddit.com/get_thread [none] — Fetch a Reddit thread by its id or URL: the post (title, text, author, score, upvote ratio, comment count, type, link) and its comments in thread order, each with author, text, score, date, permalink and nesting depth. Needs a browser signed in to Reddit. By default it returns the first page of comments Reddit shows when the thread opens; set all_comments to expand every "more replies" and get the whole tree. num_comments counts deleted and removed comments too, so the list can be shorter than that number even when it is complete. sort picks Reddit's own comment order (best, top, new, controversial, old, Q&A).
reduck/google.com/get_ai_overview [none] — Run a Google search and return the AI Overview Google shows for it: whether there is one, its answer as Markdown (headings, lists, tables and links kept), and the pages it cites, in the order the answer first cites them, each with url, title, site, byline and snippet. Google shows an AI Overview for some searches only: for the others shown is false and sources is empty. The overview changes with the country the browser is in: from two countries, the same search can cite mostly different pages. Recommended: run from the country of the people you measure for, and keep the same browser and country for every run you compare. On a managed browser, choose that country (in the US, region us-east-1); on your own browser, the country is where you are. From one place, the cited pages also change a little from run to run, so compare several runs, not one. When Google shows its anti-bot check and it cannot be cleared, the run fails and says so; this happens more often on managed browsers outside the US.
reduck/linkedin.com/get_profile [none] — Get one LinkedIn profile by its public id or profile URL: name, headline, location and its geo id, current company, About text, photo, connection degree, follower count, the stable member id, and the full lists of experience, education, languages, certifications and honors, in the order the profile shows them, with LinkedIn's ids for companies and schools and dates as month and year. Reading a profile does not record a profile view; for that reason the connection count, which only the profile page shows, is null. A role's location is the text the member saved, which can be translated or misspelled. Skills are in linkedin.com/get_profile_skills and contact details in linkedin.com/get_profile_contact_info. A field is null and a list is empty when the profile does not show it. Fails with a clear message when the browser is not signed in to LinkedIn, when the profile does not exist, or when LinkedIn limits the account.
reduck/google.com/search_places [none] — Search Google Maps for places, optionally near a location, and get the list Maps shows, in its order: name, address, phone, website, main category and all categories, star rating, number of reviews, price range, coordinates and the Google place id. Use the place id with get_place for the opening hours and with get_place_reviews for the reviews, and the coordinates with get_directions for the routes to or from a place. Google Maps lists at most 120 places for one search; complete is true when that list ended, false when cap stopped it first. A precise query that Maps opens as one place returns that one place. Category names follow hl, or the browser's language when hl is empty.
reduck/web.whatsapp.com/get_conversation [none] — Read the most recent messages of one WhatsApp chat, oldest first. Give the chat by its `chatId` from get_inbox. Each message gives its id, type, sender (in groups), time, text or caption, whether it was deleted for everyone, the delivery status of your own messages, file details for media, and its reactions with counts. `complete` is true when the start of the chat's history was reached. Reading does not open the chat, so nothing is marked as read and the other person gets no read receipt. If WhatsApp Web is open in another tab of the same browser, the run stops and asks to close that tab. If the browser is not linked to WhatsApp, the run stops and says so. An unknown chatId stops the run with an error.
reduck/community.n8n.io/get_thread_messages [none] — Read one n8n Community forum thread (community.n8n.io) by its id or url: the thread's title, category, tags, author, dates, views, likes, post count, closed and archived state and accepted answer, and its messages (posts) in thread order, 20 per page. Each message has its post number, url, author username and display name, creation and edit dates, the post it replies to, its like count, whether it is the accepted answer, and its text as Markdown (code blocks, links, images and quotes kept). Moderator actions (a thread closed, pinned, moved) are messages with an `action` code and no text. Pass `page` to read further: nextPage is null on the last page, and a page past the end returns no messages. A thread that does not exist, or is private or deleted, fails with a clear message.
reduck/meteoblue.com/get_14day_forecast [none] — 14-day weather forecast from meteoblue for one place, given its meteoblue location url (from meteoblue.com/search_locations): per day, the date, weekday, sky condition, min/max temperature in °C and meteoblue's predictability. A url meteoblue does not serve fails with that.
reduck/linkedin.com/list_inbox [none] — List or search the conversations of the classic LinkedIn messaging inbox (not Sales Navigator), 20 per page. Either pick the folder (focused, other, archived, spam) and one of the inbox filters (unread, connections, inmail, starred, jobs), newest activity first, or pass keywords to search like the inbox search box: it matches participant names, message text and conversation titles in every folder, most relevant first. Returns per conversation its thread URL and id, the other participants (name, profile URL, connection degree), whether it is read and its unread count, its categories, the last activity time and the last message (text, subject, sender, whether you sent it, attachments). Pass nextCursor as cursor, with the same other args, to read the next page. A null nextCursor or an empty page means there is nothing more. Listing does not mark any conversation as read.
reduck/airbnb.com/search_listings [none] — Search Airbnb stays in a location, with or without dates, with the filters Airbnb offers: guests, price range, room type, bedrooms, beds, bathrooms, Instant Book, guest favorites, amenities, property type, tags, host language and neighborhood (List Airbnb search filters gives their values). A map area (the north-east and south-west corners of a rectangle) limits the search to the listings inside it, as moving Airbnb's map does, for example around an office whose coordinates google.com/get_place gives. Returns one page of up to 18 listings (room id, name, price line, rating and review count, coordinates, badges, room details or next free dates, photos), the total count of matching listings, the number of pages (Airbnb stops at about 15) and the place Airbnb searched. A listing's coordinates feed google.com/get_directions for the trip to a place; Airbnb blurs them by a few hundred meters. A filter or a map area nothing matches returns an empty list. A location Airbnb cannot place fails with an error instead of returning its worldwide default list. Prices are in the currency you ask for (USD by default).
reduck/amazon.com/search-products [none] — Search Amazon by free-text query, with Amazon's own filters: department, sort order, price range, and the refinements of its left column (Prime, delivery speed, brand, customer reviews, condition, seller and the product's attributes), whose values List Amazon search filters gives. Returns one page of results: query, page, zip, url, has_next_page and items (asin, title, url, price, list_price, rating, review_count, image_url, sponsored, formats). formats lists each edition a result links to (for example Hardcover, Kindle and Audiobook for a book), with its own ASIN, URL and price when shown. has_next_page is false on the last page, on a page past the last one (Amazon stops near page 20) and when nothing matches; then Amazon can still show a few unrelated sponsored products. Organic results are stable per page but sponsored slots rotate between fetches.
reduck/reddit.com/get_subreddit_threads [none] — List a subreddit's threads by Reddit's native sort (best/hot/new/top/rising). "new" is chronological (filter with `since`); "top" takes a `time` window (hour…all); others paginate by `limit`. Returns url, title, author, score, num_comments, created, post_type, and body — the post's full text (never truncated; null for link/image posts). `limit` is a maximum, not a guarantee: fewer matching threads returns what exists.
reduck/mail.google.com/search_emails [none] — Search the signed-in Gmail with the native query syntax (from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment, after:/before:, labels…) and return matching threads: threadId (feed it to get_thread / reply_to_email), sender, senderEmail, subject, snippet, date, unread, starred, hasAttachment. Results are threads rather than individual messages, which is Gmail's own search granularity, and only the first page of results is returned (up to 50).
reduck/discord.com/read_messages [none] — Reads the most recent messages of one Discord channel or direct message, newest first, loading older ones until the requested count; complete says whether the whole history came back. Each message comes with its author, timestamp, text and edit time, its attachments (file name, link, type, size and image dimensions), its embeds and link previews (title, description, provider, image, thumbnail and video), its stickers, and the message it replies to. Attachment links expire after about a day, so download them soon. Requires being signed in. A DM or group DM is read the same way: pass its url from discord.com/list_dms. It also reads a thread or a forum post, since both are channels in their own right: pass the post's url (from discord.com/list_forum_posts). To list the posts of a forum channel rather than its messages, use discord.com/list_forum_posts. To read several channels, run the script once per channel.
reduck/reddit.com/search_reddit [none] — Search posts across all of Reddit, with Reddit's own sort and time window. Returns count and threads (id, url, title, author, subreddit, score, num_comments, created, nsfw, preview_text) in the order Reddit lists them. `limit` is a maximum: fewer matching posts return what exists, and no match returns count 0. Reddit matches loosely, so under the `top` sort a heavily upvoted post only loosely related to the query can come before closer matches; use the default `relevance` sort when on-topic results matter.
reduck/search.brave.com/submit_url [write] — Submit one URL to Brave Search to be re-crawled, and return the outcome Brave gave: whether it was accepted, plus Brave's own heading and message. Acceptance means Brave took the submission — not that the page was crawled, indexed or ranked. An invalid URL comes back as a rejection with Brave's message rather than as an error. Brave sometimes shows a rate-limit challenge here; if it does, the script raises an error — wait 30-60 seconds before retrying.
reduck/doctolib.fr/search_practitioners — Search Doctolib practitioners by specialty and location. Returns total, page, and providers with full_name, specialty, address, sector, payment_means, languages, telehealth, online_booking, matched_visit_motive, and profile_path. There are 20 providers per page and the order is server-ranked; profile_path (including ?pid=practice-N) is the join key for get_practitioner and list_slots.
reduck/x.com/search_tweets [none] — Search X (Twitter) for tweets with every X search operator, from the Top tab (a ranked sample, the default) or the Latest tab (chronological), picked by the tab arg. Returns per tweet a canonical record: id, url, author {id, handle, name}, text, created_at, lang, likes, retweets, replies, quotes, bookmarks, views, is_retweet, is_quote, plus followers (the author's follower count, a search-only enrichment), and the top-level query and count. Top is a ranked sample, not exhaustive.
reduck/welcomekit.co/get_candidate [none] — Get a candidate's full ATS profile card by their candidate reference. Returns profile and socials, cover letter, emails exchanged, event timeline, screening answers, votes, reviews, documents, other applications, and hiring/rejection fields. resumeUrl is a signed URL that expires after about 2 hours, so re-fetch it rather than storing it.

{"result": "# Reduck

Reduck automates any website through reusable browser scripts, filling the gaps where no official API exists. A script is addressed as `[<handle>/]<host>/<slug>` — discover one with `list_scripts`, read its contract with `read_script`, run it with `run_script`.

## Where scripts run

Every script runs on a **device**: a browser paired to your account through the Reduck extension. The automation inherits that browser's state — the sites you're signed into, its fingerprint — so a script that needs a login usually just works, and credentials never leave your machine. Pair from the extension's side panel; `list_devices` shows what's paired.

You can pair several browsers, each with its own device id. `browser` picks _where_ a run happens: omit it for your paired browser, `"extension"`/`"local"` to auto-pick your single device of that kind, or `{deviceId}` (equivalently the `deviceId` shorthand) to pin one — auto-pick fails if 2+ match. `"managed"` runs on a Reduck managed browser and needs a privileged account; it also takes `region`/`country`. A managed run spends browser time, and `country` additionally spends residential-proxy bandwidth — `whoami` shows both against this period's quotas.

What to run is one object: `script: {host, slug, handle?, args?}` — a script's `args` live with that script, never at the top level of the call. Each `run_script` opens a **fresh** browser.

To run several scripts, pass `scripts` — a list of those same objects, each with its own `args`. They run **at the same time, one browser each**, so this is how to fan out: one call instead of N. They share nothing (no cookies, no DOM, no order) and one failing doesn't stop the others, so you get one outcome per entry in the order you passed them, plus a `batchId`. Each entry takes its own slot on the target's concurrency budget, so more scripts than slots just queue and drain — `queued` means busy, not offline.

A run id and a batch id are different ids, and each answers for exactly one thing: `read_run_results({runId})` always reports that ONE run (its result or error) even when it belongs to a batch, while `read_run_results({batchId})` reports every script in the batch at once. Per provider, from Trustpilot (read 2026-11-09). I read the 20 most recent 1-star reviews for each provider, in all languages. Two caveats: that's a small, recent sample, and the "most common complaint" is my own tally of those 20.

NordVPN: TrustScore 4.2, 51,602 reviews (12% are 1-star). Most common complaint: unauthorized charges, surprise auto-renewals and refused refunds (about 9 of 20). Connections that don't work come a close second.

ExpressVPN: 4.4, 29,693 reviews (7% 1-star). Most common complaint: unstable VPN that won't connect or keeps dropping (about 11 of 20). Poor support and slow refunds come next.

Surfshark: 4.3, 31,815 reviews (9% 1-star). Most common complaint: auto-renewal at a higher price, with cancellation made hard and refunds refused (about 11 of 20).

Proton VPN: 2.1, 1,037 reviews (59% 1-star). Most common complaint: billing, meaning silent renewals, refunds turned into credits, and charges after cancelling (about 8 of 20). Slow or failing connections and free-tier limits are nearly as common. A few reviews attack the CEO.

CyberGhost: 4.0, 24,173 reviews (6.6% 1-star). Most common complaint: renewal overcharges and being billed early or at a higher price than advertised (about 10 of 20). Most of these reviews are not in English.

Private Internet Access: 4.2, 11,033 reviews (10% 1-star). Most common complaint: it won't connect, or the dedicated IP, ports or the app are broken (about 10 of 20). Overcharging and refunds are second (about 7 of 20). Its average reply time to negative reviews is about 27 days.

IPVanish: 3.9, 10,307 reviews (6.4% 1-star). Most common complaint: auto-renewal charged without warning or after cancelling (about 14 of 20, the clearest pattern of any provider). I queried it as www.ipvanish.com, the domain key Trustpilot uses.

Mullvad: 3.2, 192 reviews (21% 1-star). Most common complaint: payment problems, such as paying and getting no token or activation, double charges, and lost cash payments (about 8 of 20). Unresponsive support and blocked or non-working connections follow. The profile is unclaimed and has few reviews, so the score is not very reliable.

Fewest serious complaints: ExpressVPN. It has the highest TrustScore (4.4) and one of the lowest 1-star shares (7.1%). Its 1-star reviews are mostly about flaky connections and slow support, not money taken without consent. CyberGhost (6.6%) and IPVanish (6.4%) have slightly lower 1-star shares, but their complaints are almost all about billing, which I'd rate as more serious. ExpressVPN's weak spot is slow replies to negative reviews, about 6 days on average.
